title: From YOLO and Faster R-CNN to Open-Vocabulary Agents: A Survey of Object Detection and Applications
content: Object detection has moved through four overlapping eras in little more than a decade: proposal-based two-stage networks, dense single-stage regressors epitomised by the YOLO family, end-to-end detection transformers that have recently become real-time, and open-vocabulary detectors that localise arbitrary concepts described in natural language. A fifth paradigm is now emerging, in which multimodal large language models (MLLMs) either emit boxes directly or orchestrate specialised detectors as callable tools inside closed-loop, verifiable workflows. Practitioners deploying detection in manufacturing, agriculture and logistics must reason across all of these eras at once, under tight latency, power and safety constraints. This survey provides a unified, deployment-oriented account of this continuum. We (i) summarise the shared mathematical machinery—label assignment, box-regression losses, set prediction and region–text alignment-that links YOLOv1 through YOLO26, RT-DETR through RF-DETR and DEIMv2, and GLIP through DINO-X, LLMDet and SAM 3; (ii) consolidate datasets and evaluation protocols, including the fixed-AP and rare-category metrics needed to compare open-vocabulary models fairly; (iii) compile reported accuracy–latency results for more than sixty closed-set and open-vocabulary detectors together with their evaluation protocols; (iv) organise MLLM-based and agentic detection into a taxonomy of direct coordinate generation, reinforcement-tuned grounding and tool-orchestrated perception; (v) review edge-deployment techniques—re-parameterisation, low-bit quantisation, pruning, distillation and token sparsification—together with the accelerator landscape from low-power accelerators such as the Coral Edge TPU and Hailo-8 to Jetson AGX Thor; and (vi) analyse industrial inspection, precision agriculture and warehouse logistics, where zero-shot anomaly detectors and promptable detectors meet functional-safety requirements. We close with open problems in prompt robustness, long-tail calibration, certification and energy-aware perception. A continuously updated companion repository listing all surveyed papers, benchmark tables and datasets is available at https://github.com/binayksingh/Awesome-Agentic-Object-Detection.
